name: INDEX
description: INDEX returns the value at a specified position in a range or array.
tldr: INDEX retrieves a value from a specific row and column in a range.

parameters.name: array
parameters.description: The range or array from which to retrieve the value.

parameters.name: row_num
parameters.description: The row number from which to retrieve the value.

parameters.name: column_num
parameters.description: Optional. The column number from which to retrieve the value.

basicExample.explanation: Returns the value from the 3rd row and 2nd column of the range.

advancedExamples.title: INDEX with MATCH for flexible lookup
advancedExamples.description: Create a lookup that can search left
advancedExamples.explanation: Combines INDEX and MATCH for powerful two-way lookups.

howItWorks: INDEX finds the value at the intersection of the specified row and column in the range.

howToSteps.name: Select range
howToSteps.text: Define the range containing your data.

howToSteps.name: Specify row
howToSteps.text: Choose the row number to retrieve from.

howToSteps.name: Specify column
howToSteps.text: Choose the column number (optional for single-column ranges).

limitations: Row and column numbers must be within the range.
For dynamic arrays, INDEX can return multiple values.

commonErrors.fix: Check your row and column numbers.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: INDEX works identically in Google Sheets.

faq.question: Can INDEX return an entire row or column?
faq.answer: Yes, omit row_num or column_num to return an entire column or row.

faq.question: What is INDEX/MATCH?
faq.answer: INDEX/MATCH is a powerful combination that can look up values in any direction, unlike VLOOKUP.
